answer: An AI-agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a $1,000 bond for 30 days before receiving a fixed daily order quota, whether it sells plume ornaments, cipher software, or marble. Creating extra identities does not create free capacity: an attacker running 10,000 sellers must immobilize $10 million. The bond does not prove identities are unique; it makes multiplying their trading quotas costly in capital and foregone interest.
